**Finding re-submitted: deviation (INDEMN), preferred level — redline validated (ok:true, minimality ok).**

What changed in the operative text:

1. **§6.3(a)(i)** — "The Servicer will **defend and** indemnify the Issuer **and its Affiliates**, the Owner Trustee and the Indenture Trustee…" (express defence duty + affiliate coverage in the Indemnified Person definition).
2. **§6.3(a)(ii)** — "The Marketing Agent will **defend and** indemnify the Indemnified Persons…" (same duty for Cellco in its Marketing Agent capacity).
3. **New §6.3(a)(iii)** — adds the three missing triggers: violation of applicable Law; unauthorized access to or disclosure of Obligor data or Receivable Files (Cellco holds these as Custodian); and third-party claims that services or deliverables provided under the Transaction Documents infringe or misappropriate intellectual property rights.
4. **After §6.3(b)'s defence-assumption paragraph** — "The Indemnified Person will provide reasonable cooperation in the defense of the Proceeding."

Deliberately untouched, and why:
- The permissive "may participate in and assume the defense and settlement" sentence stays — it is what allocates control of the defence, and the following paragraph ("If the Servicer … notifies the Indemnified Person of its intention to assume the defense") depends on that optionality; converting it to mandatory would leave a contradictory retained mechanic.
- **No 3× super-cap** imported: §6.3 is presently uncapped, which is strictly better for us.
- **No Issuer/Depositor indemnity added**: none runs to Cellco today; §9.2 is only a narrow defence-of-title covenant, so the Customer-indemnity element is met as drafted.

Recorded in the finding: if the business confirms there is no services/deliverables, software or IP-licence subject matter in this transaction, limb (C) can be dropped as scoped out.
